title: Challenger Deep
blurb: The deepest known point of the ocean, almost 11 km down, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench where the Pacific Plate bends and sinks beneath the Mariana Plate.

title: Mid-Atlantic Ridge and Iceland
blurb: A mountain range down the middle of the Atlantic where North America and Eurasia pull apart by about 2 cm a year. At Iceland a mantle hotspot under the ridge pushes it above sea level.

title: The Hawaiian–Emperor bend
blurb: A 6,000 km trail of volcanoes made as the Pacific Plate drifted over the Hawaiian hotspot. The sharp bend, about 47 million years old, records a change in how the plate or the plume moved.

title: East Pacific Rise
blurb: The fastest-spreading major ridge: near 30° S the Pacific and Nazca plates part at about 15 cm a year, so the rise is broad and smooth instead of a deep rift valley.

title: Tonga–Kermadec Trench
blurb: The second-deepest trench, with Horizon Deep near 10.8 km. At its northern end the plates converge at up to 24 cm a year, the fastest anywhere on Earth.

title: Bahama Banks and the Great Bahama Canyon
blurb: Flat limestone platforms only a few metres deep, cut by the Tongue of the Ocean and the Great Bahama Canyon, whose walls drop more than 4 km to the abyssal plain.

title: Monterey Canyon
blurb: A submarine canyon as deep as the Grand Canyon that starts a few hundred metres off the California coast. At 1 arc-minute only its larger bends are visible; ships have mapped it at metre scale.

title: Drake Passage
blurb: The 800 km gap between South America and Antarctica. The Antarctic Circumpolar Current, the largest current on Earth, squeezes through it over the rough Shackleton and West Scotia ridges.

title: Gakkel Ridge
blurb: The slowest-spreading ridge on Earth, under 1.5 cm a year, running beneath the Arctic sea ice. Its rift valley is deep and its volcanism patchy, because so little magma reaches the surface.

title: Romanche Fracture Zone
blurb: At the equator a single transform fault shifts the Mid-Atlantic Ridge about 950 km sideways. The valley along it reaches close to 7.8 km in Vema Deep, deeper than most of the Atlantic.

title: Measured vs. estimated: the MH370 search
blurb: Between 2014 and 2017 the search for flight MH370 mapped a 120,000 km² swath of this remote seafloor in detail. Turn on “What's actually measured” to see that swath against surroundings that are only estimated from satellite gravity.
